study: Round 4 of the answer-format study: bounding the suggestion answer by its structure
question: On the demo server both suggestion requests ran into the 4,096-token output limit (about 8 s), the model walks the dish list in the given order, and the missing lists name seasonings because they are allowed values. Which request structure ends the cut-off answers and keeps latency and cost reasonable, with no numeric cutoff or fixed count in the product?

inputs.all: the 27 well-formed frozen suggestion inputs of research/experiments/dish_naive/criteria.json (expect_status 200) plus the two demo inputs below; catalog server/app/dishes/dishes.json as served (128 dishes, 18 categories)
inputs.split_subset: the split variants and S_names run on the two demo inputs plus split_sample_size inputs drawn from the 27 with random.Random(split_sample_seed).sample (fixed before any call), to stay within the call budget

variants.S_now: production: app.dishes.prompts.SUGGEST_CLOSED_SYSTEM with suggest_schema(suggest_choices(...)) over the whole dish list (same-day baseline)
variants.S_noseason: S_now with the assumed staples (server/app/dishes/staples.json plus water, with their synonym spellings) removed from the allowed missing values; the prompt text is unchanged (it already says basic seasonings are not listed)
variants.S_shuffle: S_now with the dish list (enum and user message) in a seeded random order per input, to test whether the walk in list order decides what gets listed
variants.S_names: names only (closed to the 128 names, prompt S1 of criteria.json); a cost reference only, cards would have no missing
variants.S_split: one S_now request per catalog category (the dish list's own category field; 18 groups), names closed to the group, all groups sent concurrently; answers merged, checked and ordered like the server (check_suggest, fewest_missing_first)
variants.S_split_noseason: S_split with the staples removed from the missing choices as in S_noseason

metrics: per request: truncated calls (finish_reason length; salvaged with app.dishes.answers.salvage_list), failed calls, HTTP 429 retries

per input after merging and the server's checks and ordering: dishes returned (distribution); missing per dish as written and by the rules (catalog.match) with shares 0 / 1 / 2 / 3+; share of the first five dishes with at most one rules-missing ingredient; owned ingredient listed as missing (must stay 0); share of missing items that are staples
reference recall and precision against the frozen reference definition (current catalog)
wall latency per input: single variants the call latency; split variants the measured wall time of the concurrent calls (and the slowest call); p50 and p95
input and output tokens and cost per input (sum over calls for split variants)
analysis: Descriptive, no pass/fail thresholds and no counts imposed (user rule, 2026-11-19). Report every number per variant; paired per-input differences against S_now on the inputs both ran (dishes, rules-missing mean, top-five share, recall, precision, wall latency, cost) with a percentile bootstrap 95% interval over inputs (2,000 resamples, seed 20261119). Interpret which structure removes cut-off answers while keeping latency and cost reasonable and the list close to 'what you can cook now'; implement it only if the interpretation supports it. A split by the catalog's own category field is a structural boundary, not a number.

budget.plan: S_now, S_noseason, S_shuffle on 29 inputs (87); S_names on the 8-input subset (8); S_split and S_split_noseason on the 8-input subset x 18 groups (288)
budget.retry: HTTP 429 repeated after 5 s and 15 s; every attempt counts toward the cap

limits: one run per variant at temperature 0
29 inputs for single requests, 8 for the split variants
reference sets and rules' missing counts come from the catalog's key ingredients, not from people
concurrent calls may meet provider rate limits that a sequential run does not
